summary: Glass Messenger Phase 5A (Performance Sweep) — FULLY VERIFIED. Backend 84/84 tests pass (12 new Phase5A + 72 regression Phase1-4). Frontend perf invariants all hold: exactly 1 POST per send (single + spam-guard 5 rapid clicks), typing WS frames for a 12-char burst are exactly [True, False] (NOT 12), conversation switches saved->bob->charlie->saved trigger 0 additional GET /api/conversations, emoji picker lazy-loads on first open, settings copy-username writes '@alice' to clipboard and shows the indicator, @-search hint chip still appears, and chat list ordering keeps Saved Messages pinned first.
critical_code_review_comments: list_conversations refactor in server.py (lines 514-585) is solid: single conversations.find() + single users.find($in) + single messages.aggregate($group by conversation_id) — true O(1) round trips regardless of N conversations.
Saved partition is correctly skipped when collecting other_ids and dm_conv_ids, and me_doc is fetched once and only if a saved conv exists.
Backend response shape is unchanged: id/kind/participants/other_user/last_message/last_message_at/created_at/unread_count — verified field-by-field in TestConversationsShape.

Frontend optimistic insert + sendLockRef pattern in Composer.jsx is correct: composer clears immediately (mic button replaces send button), so even raw 5x rapid clicks on the original send-button handle dispatched only 1 POST — the swap itself naturally guards subsequent clicks (defense-in-depth on top of sendLockRef).
Typing debounce is exact: 12 keystrokes produce only [True, False] over WS — confirms (a) one transition frame at idle->typing and (b) a single trailing stop frame after the 1.5s idle window.
Store-based selectors (useSyncExternalStore) work: switching active conversation never re-fetches GET /api/conversations (confirmed 0 calls across saved->bob->charlie->saved).
Emoji picker lazy-load via React.lazy + Suspense works on first open; popover appears within the 8s wait budget with no module-load errors.
Avatar.jsx loading='lazy' decoding='async' on is a free network/CPU win for long chat lists — no functional regression observed.
Backwards-compat useMessenger() shim is intentional per main agent — not flagged.
